title: Trying a new model without risking customers
summary: Run a new model beside the current one on real traffic, and decide with evidence whether it replaces it.
context: Mavalli Meals predicts delivery times. A new model looks better on last month's data, but the previous launch went badly: fine in testing, and then promises were wrong for the first rainy week. Customers are compensated when a promise is badly missed.
The team wants to run the new model silently, then on a small share of orders, and to see trouble early. The true delivery time is known only some time after a prediction is made.
must_handle: The silent model must not slow down or risk the live request.
Predictions from both can be compared with what actually happened.
Results can be split by city, weather and time of day.
A drifting input is noticed before accuracy visibly falls.
Going back to the old model takes minutes.
show_in_answer: How requests reach the two models.
How predictions are logged and joined with outcomes.
What the dashboard shows, and what raises an alarm.
The rule for moving from silent, to a small share, to everyone.
